description: Rust future drop before polling and after dispatch, followed by original rejection recovery
qualification: Local normal node built from combined unmerged source, separately built client candidate and disposable signer; not hosted or distribution qualification.
prePoll: The original call future was dropped before polling. The subsequent dispatched call produced the sole observed request stream.
limitations: Dropping a future did not return an abort receipt and is not proof of remote abort.
The post-dispatch drop occurred after durable business rejection with its response withheld, not during commit or after successful commitment.
The proxy observed one request stream and no extra queued connections; it is not a universal retry proof.
The fixture deliberately made a separate changed-input conflict probe and a distinct later business command; neither was an automatic retry.
Guest execution count was not independently measured. All later effects were acknowledged before the controlled crash.
